entries.notes: Deepest pigment of blood oranges. Ripens Dec to Mar. Color development needs cool nights below 50F. Self-fruitful. Container culture viable in zone 8 with winter shelter.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor; UF/IFAS citrus guide

windows.notes: Italian blood orange; semi-vigorous tree; harvest Feb to Apr

entries.notes: Sicilian heirloom. Largest fruit of blood oranges, mild flavor, less anthocyanin than Moro. Nearly seedless. Self-fruitful. Cultivar typical 3 to 4 yr to bear.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Spanish blood orange ripens late Feb to May; thrives inland Mediterranean climates

entries.notes: Discovered Spain 1929. Few seeds, elongated fruit, intense red rind blush. Late ripening extends harvest into May. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Florida juice orange; cold-hardier than Valencia; harvest Oct to Jan

entries.notes: Florida heirloom selected 1879. Early-season juice orange, few seeds, thin skin. More cold tolerant than most sweet oranges (briefly to 26F). Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension citrus cultivar guide; USDA GRIN

windows.notes: Mid-season Florida juice orange; ripens Dec to Feb

entries.notes: Florida heirloom circa 1860. Aromatic pineapple-scented juice, many seeds (15 to 25), rich flavor. Self-fruitful but tends to alternate bear.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension citrus cultivar guide

windows.notes: Early Florida juice orange; harvest Sep to Jan

entries.notes: Florida heirloom 1856. Earliest commercial juice orange, many seeds, rough rind. Largely replaced by Hamlin commercially. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension citrus cultivar guide

windows.notes: Late-season navel extending harvest 2 to 4 months past Washington navel

entries.notes: Australian bud sport of Washington navel discovered 1950. Smaller navel, holds on tree to June without losing quality. Self-fruitful seedless.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Cold-hardiest commercial mandarin (briefly to 18F when dormant); ideal Gulf Coast

entries.notes: Japanese heirloom. Seedless, easy-peel, ripens Oct to Dec. Hardiest sweet citrus for zone 8b. Self-fruitful. Move container plants to shelter below 20F.
entries.source: LSU AgCenter satsuma fact sheet; UF/IFAS citrus guide

windows.notes: Classic Christmas tangerine; harvest Dec to Feb

entries.notes: Florida heirloom 1867. Deep red-orange zipper-skin tangerine, many seeds when cross-pollinated. Tends to alternate bear. Self-fruitful but heavier with pollinizer.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension citrus cultivar guide

windows.notes: Ojai Valley specialty; very late ripening Mar to Jun

entries.notes: UC Riverside release 1965. Seedless, easy-peel, small pebbly fruit, sweet. Alternate bearer, prune annually. Isolate from seedy mandarins. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Late-season seedless mandarin; harvest Feb to Jun

entries.notes: UC Riverside release 1999. Seedless, pebbly rind, holds long on tree without losing sweetness. Self-fruitful. Excellent container variety.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Distinctive top-knot fruit; needs heat to develop sweetness; harvest Feb to Apr

entries.notes: Japanese hybrid (Kiyomi x Ponkan). Large bumpy fruit with neck, very sweet, easy peel, seedless. Cold-sensitive young; protect below 28F.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Heavy bearer; harvest Nov to Feb

entries.notes: USDA Orlando 1942 hybrid (Minneola tangelo x Clementine). Small juicy fruit, few seeds when isolated, rich flavor. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: USDA GRIN germplasm descriptor; UF/IFAS citrus guide

windows.notes: Very sweet small fruit; harvest Jan to Mar; alternate bearer

entries.notes: Originally Murcott bud sport. Smaller than Murcott, intensely sweet, easy peel, many seeds when cross-pollinated. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Classic clementine; isolate from other mandarins to keep seedless

entries.notes: North African heirloom. Seedless when grown alone, easy peel, mild sweet, harvest Nov to Jan. Cross-pollination introduces seeds.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Marketed as Delite or Tango when seedless; isolate or use Tango clone

entries.notes: Moroccan selection. Easy peel, deep orange, very sweet, harvest Jan to Apr. Tango is irradiated seedless clone. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Very late season mandarin; harvest Apr to Jul

entries.notes: UC Riverside 1965 release. Latest mandarin, holds on tree all summer. Many seeds, freckled rind, intense flavor. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Needs cross-pollinizer (Kinnow or Dancy) for heavy crop; harvest Nov to Jan

entries.notes: USDA Indio 1964 hybrid (Clementine x Orlando tangelo). Deep orange, juicy, many seeds, requires pollinizer for full yield.

windows.notes: Vigorous Pakistani staple; very heat tolerant; harvest Jan to Apr

entries.notes: UC Riverside 1935 hybrid (King x Willowleaf). Tall vigorous tree, many seeds, rich flavor, holds long. Heat-loving. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Bell-shaped neck; cross-pollinize with Dancy or Clementine for heavy crop

entries.notes: USDA 1931 cross (Duncan grapefruit x Dancy tangerine). Distinctive neck, deep red-orange, tart-sweet. Self-fruitful but pollinizer boosts yield.
entries.source: USDA GRIN germplasm descriptor; UF/IFAS citrus guide

windows.notes: Sibling of Minneola; earlier ripening Nov to Jan; needs Temple or mandarin pollinizer

entries.notes: USDA 1931 sibling of Minneola. Flatter fruit, sweeter, fewer seeds with pollinizer. Slightly hardier than Minneola.

windows.notes: Year-round bearer in coastal CA; thornless; the supermarket lemon

entries.notes: Sicilian seedling selected California 1858. Open canopy, nearly thornless, ever-bearing in mild climates. Self-fruitful. Less cold-hardy than Lisbon.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor; UC ANR citrus production manual

windows.notes: Dense thorny tree, cold and heat tolerant; main winter crop

entries.notes: Portuguese origin, prominent in Australia and Arizona. Vigorous thorny tree, heavier winter crop than Eureka, hardier to 26F briefly. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Massive grapefruit-sized lemons; ornamental container plant

entries.notes: Lemon-citron hybrid 1887. Huge thick-rind fruit up to 2 lb, mild lemon flavor. Compact tree, popular conservatory plant. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Variegated foliage and green-striped fruit; pink flesh; ornamental

entries.notes: Eureka bud sport. Variegated white and green leaves, fruit with green stripes ripening yellow, pink-tinted flesh. Self-fruitful. Slightly less vigorous.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Italian limoncello lemon; very productive 4 crops per year

entries.notes: Group of Italian heirloom lemons (Femminello Comune, Siracusano). Up to four flushes annually, used for limoncello. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: PGI Italian limoncello lemon; thick aromatic rind; harvest Feb to May

entries.notes: Femminello Ovale clone, PGI from Sorrento peninsula Italy. Thick fragrant rind ideal for limoncello, juicy flesh. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Vigorous rootstock and fruit; orange-red rind; salt and lime tolerant

entries.notes: Italian rough lemon-sour orange hybrid. Productive, edible orange-tinted lemon, also widely used as rootstock for tolerance to high pH and calcareous soils.

windows.notes: New Zealand Lisbon selection; thin smooth skin; high juice content

entries.notes: Australian-New Zealand Lisbon bud sport. Smaller smoother fruit than Lisbon, thin rind, very juicy, few seeds. Compact tree. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Thorny shrub; tolerates partial shade; harvest Aug to Feb

entries.notes: Australian rainforest native. Cylindrical fruit with crisp caviar-like vesicles, colors range green to pink to red. Slow to bear, 4 to 5 yr. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Looks like a tangerine, tastes like a lime; also a rootstock

entries.notes: Indian mandarin-lemon hybrid. Orange rind and flesh, intensely acidic lime flavor, very productive. Drought and cold tolerant. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Non-acidic lime; insipid sweet flavor; medicinal traditional use

entries.notes: Middle Eastern sweet lime. Yellow at maturity, low acid, sweet bland flavor used medicinally. Vigorous, productive. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Mediterranean sweet lime distinct from Palestinian; low acid yellow fruit

entries.notes: Mediterranean species, often confused with Palestinian sweet lime. Round yellow fruit, low acid, mildly sweet. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: White-flesh seedless grapefruit; needs heat for sweetness; harvest Dec to May

entries.notes: Florida 1860 chance seedling. Seedless white flesh, classic grapefruit acidity, holds long on tree. Needs heat units for quality. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Deepest red flesh; herbicide-sensitive; harvest Jan to May

entries.notes: Texas A&M 1971 release, mutation of Hudson. Deepest red flesh, seedless, smaller tree than Marsh, herbicide-sensitive. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: Texas A&M AgriLife grapefruit cultivar guide

windows.notes: Texas commercial red grapefruit; harvest Nov to Apr

entries.notes: Texas 1984 mutation of Ruby Red. Deeper red flesh than Ruby, retains color longer, seedless, more vigorous than Star Ruby. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: Texas A&M AgriLife grapefruit cultivar guide

windows.notes: Sweet low-acid grapefruit hybrid; thick rind; harvest Dec to Feb

entries.notes: UC Riverside 1981 release, pummelo x white grapefruit. Seedless, sweet without grapefruit bitterness, thick spongy rind. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Sibling of Oroblanco; larger fruit; harvest Dec to Feb

entries.notes: UC Riverside 1986 release, sibling of Oroblanco. Larger fruit, thinner rind, slightly more grapefruit character. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Largest citrus fruit; pink flesh; thick rind candy-able; harvest Nov to Feb

entries.notes: UC Riverside 1961 release. Massive fruit (5 to 8 lb), pink flesh, low acid, sweet, thick rind. Self-fruitful but slow to bear (5 to 7 yr).
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Japanese pummelo; pinkish white flesh; very sweet

entries.notes: Japanese heirloom from Hirado Island. Large fruit, pinkish flesh, sweeter and lower acid than Chandler. Slow to bear. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Cold-hardy citrus (briefly to 18F dormant); compact for containers

entries.notes: Oval kumquat, sweet edible rind tart flesh, ripens Nov to Mar. Most common kumquat. Self-fruitful. Excellent in containers in cold-winter zones.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor; UF/IFAS kumquat guide

windows.notes: Sweetest kumquat; round fruit; eat whole; harvest Dec to Apr

entries.notes: Sweet kumquat hybrid. Round fruit, thicker sweeter rind, less tart flesh than Nagami. Best eaten whole fresh. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Round kumquat; slightly hardier than Nagami; thorny tree

entries.notes: Round kumquat, sweet rind tart flesh, thornier and slightly hardier than Nagami. Self-fruitful. Good preserves.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Thornless kumquat with broad leaves; sweet rind sweet flesh; container friendly

entries.notes: Japanese kumquat-mandarin hybrid. Thornless, broad leaves, sweet rind and sweet flesh, slightly larger than other kumquats. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Fingered ornamental citron; rind only, no juice; very frost sensitive

entries.notes: Citron variety with finger-like segments, all rind no flesh, intensely fragrant. Used as zest, candied peel, and ceremonial offering. Sensitive below 30F.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Ritual Jewish citron; pitam tip preserved; very frost sensitive

entries.notes: Ritual citron used in Sukkot. Bumpy yellow fruit, thick aromatic rind, small dry pulp. Multiple regional strains (Moroccan, Yemenite, Diamante). Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Calabrian aromatic citrus; rind oil for Earl Grey and perfumery

entries.notes: Probable lemon-sour orange hybrid. Pear-shaped sour fruit, rind oil flavoring Earl Grey tea and perfumes. Calabria Italy produces 90 percent of world supply. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Marmalade orange; also a major rootstock; fragrant white flowers

entries.notes: Bitter orange. Very sour and bitter fruit used for marmalade, curacao, Cuban mojo. Also widely used as rootstock. Very fragrant blossom for orange flower water. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Hardiest citrus relative (zone 5b briefly); deciduous; primary rootstock

entries.notes: Deciduous citrus relative hardy to minus 10F. Small fuzzy aromatic fruit, inedible raw, used for marmalade. Primary commercial rootstock. Self-fruitful. Cold tolerance unmatched.
entries.source: USDA GRIN germplasm descriptor; UGA Cooperative Extension cold-hardy citrus

windows.notes: Major rootstock; tart edible fruit; cold tolerant to 12F when dormant

entries.notes: USDA 1909 cross of Washington navel x trifoliate orange. Primary citrus rootstock worldwide. Sour edible fruit used for lemonade-like drink. Cold-hardier than commercial citrus.

windows.notes: Mexican lime x kumquat; cold-hardier than true lime; container friendly

entries.notes: USDA 1909 cross of Mexican lime x Marumi kumquat. Small yellow fruit, tart lime flavor, edible rind. Hardier than true lime, briefly to 22F. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Type A flower; pair with Type B (Fuerte, Bacon) for heavier crop; harvest Feb to Sep

entries.notes: Guatemalan-Mexican hybrid, 1935 California seedling. Dominant commercial cultivar. Pebbly rind turns black ripe, creamy rich flesh, 18 percent oil. Hardy to 30F. Self-fruitful but pollinizer boosts yield.

windows.notes: Type B flower; cold tolerant to 24F; good Hass pollinizer

entries.notes: Mexican-Guatemalan hybrid, California 1954. Smooth green skin, light watery flesh, hardier than Hass. Excellent Type B pollinizer for Hass. Harvest Nov to Mar.

windows.notes: Type A flower; pear-shaped elongated fruit; small seed

entries.notes: Guatemalan, California 1972. Long pear shape, small seed, high oil content, slightly pebbly skin, harvest Nov to Apr. Less cold tolerant than Hass.

windows.notes: Type A flower; round summer-ripening avocado; upright compact tree

entries.notes: Guatemalan, California 1948. Round green-skinned fruit, large, creamy rich, harvest Jul to Sep. Upright compact tree fits smaller yards.

windows.notes: Type A flower; Gwen seedling; later season than Hass; harvest Apr to Nov

entries.notes: California 1979 seedling. Larger fruit than Hass, similar quality, upright compact tree, more heat tolerant, ripens later than Hass extending season.

windows.notes: Type A flower; hardiest Mexican race avocado; briefly to 18F

entries.notes: Pure Mexican race, California 1910. Small black-skinned thin-rind fruit, anise-scented leaves, harvest Aug to Oct. Cold-hardy briefly to 18F. Edible skin.

windows.notes: Type B flower; Texas cold-hardy Mexican race; briefly to 15F

entries.notes: Texas seedling from Uvalde. Mexican race, very cold-hardy briefly to 15F, dark purple-black thin skin, nutty flavor, harvest Aug to Sep. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: Texas A&M AgriLife avocado for South Texas

windows.notes: Type A flower; cold-hardy Texas selection briefly to 15F

entries.notes: Texas cold-hardy Mexican race seedling. Green-skinned medium fruit, harvest Aug to Oct, briefly to 15F. Compact tree suited to North Texas. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: Texas A&M AgriLife avocado for South Texas

windows.notes: Type B flower; Florida West Indian x Mexican; purple skin

entries.notes: Florida cold-hardy hybrid. Purple-black skin, mild flavor, harvest Aug to Oct. Hardier than most Florida avocados. Type B pollinizer.

windows.notes: Type B flower; Mexican-Guatemalan cold-hardy; semi-dwarf tree

entries.notes: California seedling. Green pear-shaped fruit, semi-dwarf habit suiting small yards or large containers, cold-hardy briefly to 24F, harvest Aug to Oct.

windows.notes: Indian premium mango; alternate bearer; harvest May to Jun in tropics

entries.notes: Konkan India heirloom, the Hapus or king of mangoes. Saffron-yellow flesh, rich aromatic, very alternate bearing. Single embryonic (monoembryonic). Frost-sensitive below 30F.
entries.source: ICAR India mango cultivar guide; UF/IFAS tropical fruit guide

windows.notes: Gujarat saffron mango; harvest Apr to Jun in tropics

entries.notes: Gujarat India heirloom. Saffron-orange flesh, sweet aromatic, slightly fibrous, monoembryonic. Frost-sensitive. Excellent for pulp and aamras.

windows.notes: Florida late-season green-when-ripe; small dwarfable tree; harvest Aug to Oct

entries.notes: Florida 1939 seedling. Large green-blushed fruit even when ripe, fiberless flesh, very late season. Polyembryonic. Slightly anthracnose-resistant. Briefly to 30F mature.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida fiberless commercial; medium-late; harvest Jul to Sep

entries.notes: Florida 1944 Brooks seedling. Large yellow-flushed red fruit, fiberless rich flesh, monoembryonic, alternate bearer in subtropics. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Dominant supermarket cultivar; firm shipping fruit; harvest May to Jul

entries.notes: Florida 1922 Haden seedling. Red-blushed firm flesh, ships well, monoembryonic, anthracnose-tolerant. Fiber and modest flavor versus Alphonso. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Parent of many Florida cultivars; harvest Jun to Jul; alternate bearer

entries.notes: Florida 1910 Mulgoba seedling. Original commercial Florida mango, parent of Kent, Tommy Atkins, Keitt. Yellow-red blushed, mildly fibrous, monoembryonic.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida dooryard favorite; mild non-fibrous flesh; harvest Jun to Jul

entries.notes: Florida 1940s Saigon seedling. Sweet mild non-fibrous flesh, reliable bearer, monoembryonic. Good first mango for newcomers, less acidic. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida dwarfing condo mango; harvest Jun to Jul

entries.notes: Florida 1940 seedling. Small compact tree (10 to 15 ft), green when ripe, rich aromatic flesh with slight resin note, monoembryonic. Container-friendly.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida dwarfing condo cultivar; fits 8 ft pot trees; harvest Jun to Jul

entries.notes: Florida Haden seedling. Naturally dwarf habit, ideal container or small-yard. Yellow red-blushed fruit, mild sweet fiberless flesh, monoembryonic.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Indian Neelum x Dasheri hybrid; bears young; harvest Jun to Jul

entries.notes: ICAR India 1971 cross (Neelum x Dasheri). Bears young 2 to 3 yr, semi-dwarf, intensely aromatic citrus-honey notes, fiberless, monoembryonic.

windows.notes: Mexican Philippine-type honey mango; small yellow fruit; harvest Apr to Jun

entries.notes: Mexican selection of Philippine Carabao type. Small flat yellow fruit, very sweet honey-like flesh, thin papery seed, polyembryonic, comes true from seed.
entries.source: UF/IFAS tropical fruit guide; SAGARPA Mexico mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Thai sweet long fruit; eaten green-ripe; harvest Jun to Jul

entries.notes: Thai heirloom. Long elongated bright yellow fruit, very sweet fiberless flesh, polyembryonic, eaten green or fully ripe. Compact growth.

windows.notes: Florida late-season Haden seedling; large elongated fruit; harvest Jul to Aug

entries.notes: Florida Haden seedling 1937. Large elongated yellow-orange fruit, fiberless rich flesh, monoembryonic, vigorous tree. Reliable bearer.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Pink-fleshed dessert guava; bears in 2 yr; protect below 28F

entries.notes: Pink-fleshed sweet tropical guava, large fruit, low seed count, low acidity. Bears young, two crops per year in mild winters. Hardy briefly to 27F mature.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension guava cultivar guide

windows.notes: Cream-fleshed dessert guava; very sweet; vigorous tree

entries.notes: Mexican heirloom. Cream-white flesh, very sweet floral aroma, small to medium fruit, low acid. Vigorous productive tree. Container-friendly with pruning.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension guava cultivar guide

windows.notes: Red-fleshed Florida guava; large fruit; balanced sweet-tart

entries.notes: Florida selection. Red-pink flesh, large round fruit, balanced sweet-tart flavor, productive. Hardy briefly to 27F mature.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension guava cultivar guide

windows.notes: Hawaiian commercial pink-flesh; juice and jelly use

entries.notes: U Hawaii 1965 release. Pink flesh, large fruit, mildly acidic ideal for juice processing and jelly. Heavy bearer. Excellent disease resistance.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR guava cultivar guide

windows.notes: Indian white-flesh table guava; high vitamin C; very sweet

entries.notes: Indian heirloom from Uttar Pradesh. White flesh, very sweet, soft texture, small seeds. Premier table guava in India. Heavy bearer in subtropics.

windows.notes: Red-flesh Mexican commercial; large fruit 4 to 8 lb; dioecious

entries.notes: Cuban-Mexican commercial variety. Large red-flesh fruit, sweet musky flavor. Dioecious, plant 5 to 10 for male and hermaphrodite mix. Frost kills at 32F.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR papaya cultivar guide; SAGARPA Mexico papaya guide

windows.notes: Hawaiian single-serve papaya; red-orange flesh; hermaphrodite seed

entries.notes: U Hawaii 1959 release from Solo line. Small (1 to 2 lb) personal-size, red-orange flesh, sweet rich flavor. Hermaphrodite seed produces 67 percent hermaphrodites.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR papaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Sunrise sibling; sweeter slightly smaller fruit

entries.notes: U Hawaii Solo selection. Slightly smaller and sweeter than Sunrise Solo, red flesh, hermaphrodite seed predominant. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR papaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Hawaiian Solo with thick wall and small seed cavity

entries.notes: U Hawaii 1968 release. Solo type, orange-yellow flesh, thick walls, small cavity, firm texture good for shipping. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR papaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Taiwanese hybrid; red flesh; vigorous productive

entries.notes: Taiwan release. Red flesh, large (2 to 4 lb) elongated fruit, sweet, vigorous productive. Used widely in Caribbean and Mexico commercial production.
entries.source: Taiwan TAES papaya cultivar guide; UF/IFAS tropical fruit guide

windows.notes: Known-You F1 hybrid; tolerant to PRSV; precocious bearer

entries.notes: Known-You Seed Taiwan F1 hybrid. Red flesh, oblong 2 to 4 lb fruit, sweet, tolerant of papaya ringspot virus, bears at 3 ft tall. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: Known-You Seed papaya descriptor; UF/IFAS tropical fruit guide

windows.notes: Vigorous vine; needs sturdy trellis; self-fruitful; harvest summer to fall

entries.notes: Classic purple passionfruit. Bears 12 to 18 months from planting, sweet-tart pulp, dies back at 30F but regrows from roots in zone 9. Trellis 8 to 10 ft.
entries.source: UC ANR passionfruit production guide; UF/IFAS tropical fruit guide

windows.notes: Burbank purple cultivar; compact for containers; self-fruitful

entries.notes: Luther Burbank selection. Smaller more compact vine than typical purple, suited to containers and small trellises, dark purple aromatic fruit. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Eastern US native; cold-hardy to minus 20F; herbaceous perennial returns each spring

entries.notes: North American native passionflower. Yellow-green fruit ripens summer, edible aromatic pulp, vine dies back annually in cold zones and regrows from roots. Pollinator magnet.
entries.source: USDA NRCS plant fact sheet; SE native plant guide

windows.notes: Andean cool-tropical species; prefers mild not hot climates; 3500 to 7000 ft elevation

entries.notes: Andean species, prized in Colombia. Orange-yellow fruit, sweet low-acid pulp, brittle shell. Needs cool nights and partial shade. Frost-sensitive below 32F.

windows.notes: Florida commercial cultivar; needs winter chill 100 to 200 hr below 68F for flowering

entries.notes: Florida 1903 import from Fujian China. Large bright red fruit, sweet aromatic, sometimes chicken-tongue (aborted) seed. Needs cool winters to flower. Alternate bearer.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension lychee cultivar guide

windows.notes: Reliable bearer in tropics; early to mid-season; harvest May to Jun

entries.notes: Florida and South Africa commercial. Red-rose fruit, sweet juicy aril, large seed. More reliable bearer than Brewster in warm winters. Frost-sensitive young.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension lychee cultivar guide

windows.notes: Chinese black leaf premium cultivar; high chicken-tongue seed rate

entries.notes: Chinese heirloom (Hei Ye, Black Leaf). Premium quality, high rate of small aborted seed, sweet aromatic flesh, dark red leathery rind. Needs chill to flower.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR lychee cultivar guide

windows.notes: Australian commercial cultivar; mid-season; small seed; reliable bearer

entries.notes: Australian commercial lychee. Pink-red small to medium fruit, sweet aromatic, often small seed, reliable bearer in subtropics. Needs chill to flower.

windows.notes: Florida precocious longan; flowers without cool winter; harvest Jul to Aug

entries.notes: Florida selection. Flowers more reliably than Kohala without chill, weeping form, smaller fruit. Good Florida and South Texas variety. Frost-sensitive young.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension longan cultivar guide

windows.notes: Hawaii commercial standard; large sweet fruit; needs slight chill

entries.notes: U Hawaii 1955 release. Large bronze-brown fruit, sweet juicy aril, small seed, vigorous tree. Slight chill required for reliable cropping.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR longan cultivar guide

windows.notes: Thai commercial cultivar; large premium fruit

entries.notes: Thai commercial standard. Large fruit, thick crisp aril, small seed, sweet. Most planted longan in Thailand. Needs warm winters not cold.

windows.notes: Australian-bred crunchy-firm fleshed cultivar; bears 3 yr; cauliflorous

entries.notes: Australian selection. Firm orange flesh, sweet, holds shape when cooked, medium size 10 to 30 lb. Bears young, reliable. Frost kills below 32F.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension jackfruit cultivar guide

windows.notes: Australian jackfruit x champedak hybrid; smaller fruit; intensely aromatic

entries.notes: Australian-bred hybrid of jackfruit and champedak. Smaller fruit (5 to 15 lb), intensely aromatic, sweet rich flavor. Earlier bearing than standard jackfruit.

windows.notes: Malaysian commercial cultivar; bears young; crisp orange flesh

entries.notes: Malaysian commercial release. Crisp deep orange flesh, sweet, small seeds, bears young at 2 to 3 yr from grafted plant. Frost-sensitive.

windows.notes: Australian selection; bright lemon-yellow firm flesh; sweet

entries.notes: Australian selection. Bright lemon-yellow firm-crisp flesh, very sweet, medium size, holds well in storage. Bears 3 to 4 yr from grafted plant.

windows.notes: Yellow-flesh dessert loquat; blooms in fall; flowers killed below 27F

entries.notes: California heirloom. Pale yellow juicy sweet flesh, large fruit. Flowers Nov to Jan, fruit ripens Mar to May. Tree hardy to 10F but flowers die below 27F.
entries.source: UC ANR loquat cultivar guide; UF/IFAS loquat guide

windows.notes: Late-season orange-flesh loquat; large fruit; firm dessert quality

entries.notes: California 1880 origin. Orange flesh, large fruit, slightly tart-sweet, late ripening Apr to Jun, ships better than most. Self-fruitful but pollinizer boosts yield.

windows.notes: White-flesh self-fertile pitaya; needs sturdy trellis; protect below 32F

entries.notes: Vietnamese commercial white-flesh dragonfruit. Self-fertile, large pink-skinned fruit, mild sweet flesh. Climbing cactus needs trellis. Hardy briefly to 28F established.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension pitaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Red-flesh self-fertile; sweet rich flavor; harvest Jul to Nov

entries.notes: Florida selection. Self-fertile red-flesh dragonfruit, sweet flavor with berry notes, productive. Needs trellis 6 to 8 ft.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension pitaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Red-flesh prolific bearer; sweet kiwi-strawberry notes

entries.notes: Florida selection. Red-flesh, very prolific, large fruit with sweet kiwi-strawberry flavor notes. Self-fertile. Pollination by hand boosts size.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension pitaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Pink-flesh sweetest commonly grown variety; small fruit

entries.notes: Florida selection. Pink-magenta flesh, sweetest dragonfruit commonly available, small fruit (4 to 8 oz). Self-fertile. Excellent dessert quality.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension pitaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Yellow-skin white-flesh; sweetest of all pitayas; slow ripening 5 to 6 months

entries.notes: Colombian-Ecuadoran species. Yellow spiny skin, white flesh, exceptionally sweet (highest brix of pitayas), slow ripening. Self-fertile but hand-pollinate. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension pitaya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida sweet commercial carambola; bears 2 to 3 yr; multiple crops per year

entries.notes: Florida 1965 release. Sweet large yellow ribbed fruit, low oxalic acid, productive, dwarfs to 12 ft. Several crops per year in tropics. Frost tender below 28F.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension carambola cultivar guide

windows.notes: Hawaiian sweet selection; very productive; thin-rib fruit

entries.notes: U Hawaii release. Very sweet thin-ribbed fruit, productive, slightly smaller than Arkin. Frost-sensitive. Good Florida and Hawaii dooryard tree.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR carambola cultivar guide

windows.notes: California heirloom; needs hand pollination; harvest Nov to Apr

entries.notes: California heirloom. Medium fruit, sweet papaya-banana flavor, productive, often requires hand pollination with paintbrush. Hardy briefly to 26F mature.

windows.notes: California selection; sweetest commonly grown cherimoya

entries.notes: California heirloom. Heart-shaped fruit, exceptionally sweet creamy flesh, hand pollination required for reliable crops. Excellent dessert quality.

windows.notes: California heirloom; smaller fruit; bears young; self-pollinating tendency

entries.notes: California heirloom. Smaller smoother fruit than Booth or Whaley, slight self-pollinating tendency, sweet aromatic flesh. Productive in coastal California.

windows.notes: Spanish commercial cultivar; large smooth fruit; few seeds

entries.notes: Spanish commercial standard, Granada Spain. Large smooth-skinned fruit, sweet creamy white flesh, few seeds, productive. Hand pollination boosts yield.

windows.notes: Israeli commercial standard; self-pollinating tendency; bears young

entries.notes: Israeli release 1970s, cherimoya x sugar apple cross. Self-pollinating tendency reduces hand work, sweet vanilla-pineapple flavor, productive. Frost-sensitive.
entries.source: Israel ARO atemoya cultivar guide; UF/IFAS atemoya guide

windows.notes: South African commercial; heart-shaped fruit; bears 2 to 3 yr

entries.notes: South African selection. Heart-shaped fruit, smooth skin, creamy sweet flesh, productive, slightly tart compared to Geffner. Hand pollination boosts yield.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension atemoya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida heirloom selection; smooth-skinned heart shape; sweet

entries.notes: Florida heirloom. Smooth-skinned heart-shaped fruit, sweet creamy flesh, productive in subtropics. Frost-sensitive below 30F.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension atemoya cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida selection; conical fruit; very sweet pineapple notes

entries.notes: Florida selection. Conical fruit, smooth pebbly skin, very sweet pineapple-tinged flesh. Less productive than Geffner but better flavor in many opinions.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension atemoya cultivar guide

windows.notes: California precocious bearer; flowers and fruits year-round; semi-self-fruitful

entries.notes: California selection. Bears young at 3 yr, often ever-bearing in mild climates, custard-sweet flesh, partly self-fruitful. Hardy briefly to 22F.
entries.source: UC ANR white sapote cultivar guide

windows.notes: California Pike seedling; cold-hardy; large fruit; rich flavor

entries.notes: California Pike seedling, considered one of the best-flavored white sapotes. Large fruit, rich sweet flesh, vigorous tree, hardy briefly to 22F.
entries.source: UC ANR white sapote cultivar guide

windows.notes: Florida heavy bearer; large fruit; chocolate pudding fruit; pollination by male persimmon helps

entries.notes: Florida selection. Large fruit, dense chocolate-pudding-textured dark flesh when ripe, mildly sweet. Frost-sensitive below 30F. Pollination boosts crop.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension black sapote guide

windows.notes: Eaten yellow-khalal stage crisp like apple; soft when fully ripe; needs hot dry summer

entries.notes: Iraqi heirloom soft date. Eaten yellow-crisp at khalal stage (apple-like) or soft rutab/tamr stage. Female palm needs male pollinizer or hand pollination.
entries.source: UC ANR date palm production manual

windows.notes: Soft date; high yields; honey-caramel sweetness

entries.notes: Iraqi heirloom soft date. High yields, soft honey-caramel sweet flesh, smaller than Medjool. Hand pollinate from male palm. Hardy briefly to 20F.
entries.source: UC ANR date palm production manual

windows.notes: Dry semi-dry date; long shelf life; eaten at khalal yellow stage

entries.notes: Iraqi heirloom dry date. Long shelf life, golden firm flesh, nutty buttery flavor, lower sugar than soft dates. Cold-hardy briefly to 20F.
entries.source: UC ANR date palm production manual

windows.notes: Caribbean F1 hybrid resistant to lethal yellowing; semi-dwarf; bears 6 to 7 yr

entries.notes: Jamaica 1974 hybrid (Malayan Dwarf x Panama Tall). Resistant to lethal yellowing disease, semi-dwarf habit (40 to 60 ft), reliable bearer.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension coconut palm guide

windows.notes: Dwarf bears at 4 to 6 yr; small stature 25 to 30 ft; yellow husk fruit

entries.notes: Malaysian dwarf. Compact 25 to 30 ft tree bears at 4 to 6 yr. Yellow-husked nuts, sweet water, popular landscape palm in tropics.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension coconut palm guide

windows.notes: Fijian dwarf; extremely short stature 15 to 20 ft; bears young

entries.notes: Fijian dwarf, smallest commercial coconut palm at 15 to 20 ft. Bears at 3 to 4 yr, medium fruit, suitable for small tropical gardens.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR coconut palm guide

windows.notes: Thai sweet tamarind; lower acid than commercial; eaten fresh

entries.notes: Thai sweet selection (Manila Sweet, Sri Tong). Lower acid, eaten fresh like a fruit, not just used for cooking. Slow grower, bears at 5 to 6 yr. Hardy briefly to 28F mature.

windows.notes: Commercial sour tamarind; used in chutneys, sauces, drinks; very productive

entries.notes: Standard sour tamarind. Tart paste used for pad thai, chutneys, Worcestershire sauce, agua fresca. Large long-lived tree, very productive. Long-lived 150+ yr.

windows.notes: Sweet Barbados cherry; highest vitamin C of common fruits; multiple crops per year

entries.notes: Florida sweet selection. Red cherry-like fruit, exceptionally high vitamin C (1500+ mg per 100g), 2 to 4 crops per year in mild climates. Hardy briefly to 28F.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension acerola cultivar guide

windows.notes: Classic specialty cultivar; complex sweet cup; lower yield than commodity

entries.notes: Bourbon Island heirloom from Reunion. Sweeter more complex cup than Typica, productive in shade, susceptible to leaf rust. Pink, red, and yellow Bourbon variants exist.
entries.source: World Coffee Research arabica variety catalog

windows.notes: Original arabica variety; clean cup; low yield; tall conical tree

entries.notes: The original arabica spread from Yemen. Tall conical form, low yield but excellent clean cup, basis of Jamaica Blue Mountain and Hawaii Kona. Susceptible to disease.
entries.source: World Coffee Research arabica variety catalog

windows.notes: Dwarf Bourbon mutation; high yield; suited to dense plantings

entries.notes: Brazilian Bourbon mutation discovered 1937. Compact dwarf form (4 to 6 ft), high yield, suited to dense plantings, slightly less complex than Bourbon. Container friendly.
entries.source: World Coffee Research arabica variety catalog

windows.notes: Brazilian commercial standard; Bourbon x Typica hybrid; vigorous

entries.notes: Brazilian natural hybrid (Bourbon x Sumatra Typica), 1940s. Vigorous tall productive, balanced cup, foundation of Brazilian coffee industry. Some leaf rust resistance.
entries.source: World Coffee Research arabica variety catalog

windows.notes: Kenyan Scott Labs selection; cup signature blackcurrant; drought tolerant

entries.notes: Kenya Scott Labs 1935 release. Drought tolerant, exceptional cup quality with blackcurrant and citrus, low yield, susceptible to coffee leaf rust. Specialty favorite.
entries.source: World Coffee Research arabica variety catalog

windows.notes: Ethiopian heirloom; bergamot-jasmine cup; specialty premium; low yield

entries.notes: Ethiopian heirloom (Gesha region), brought to Panama 1960s. Sets record auction prices. Floral jasmine-bergamot cup, low yield, tall sparse tree, needs altitude for top flavor.
entries.source: World Coffee Research arabica variety catalog

windows.notes: Larger fatter pods than planifolia; less aromatic; heliotropin notes

entries.notes: West Indian vanilla species. Larger fatter pods, less vanillin and more heliotropin, marketed as vanillon. Needs host tree and hand pollination. Frost kills.
entries.source: USDA GRIN germplasm descriptor; FAO vanilla cultivation guide

windows.notes: True cinnamon; bark harvested at 2 to 3 yr from coppiced shoots; multi-stem shrub

entries.notes: Sri Lankan native, true cinnamon. Bark of 2 to 3 yr shoots harvested from coppiced bush. Lower coumarin than cassia, mild sweet flavor. Frost-sensitive below 35F.
entries.source: FAO cinnamon cultivation guide; Sri Lanka EDB cinnamon descriptor

windows.notes: Chinese cinnamon; common supermarket spice; hardier than Ceylon

entries.notes: Chinese-origin cinnamon, dominant supermarket type. Stronger spicier flavor, higher coumarin (limit intake), thicker bark, hardier than Ceylon briefly to 32F.

windows.notes: Brazilian commercial jaboticaba; small fruit on trunk; bears 7 to 10 yr from seed

entries.notes: Brazilian Cerrado native. Grape-like dark purple fruit directly on trunk (cauliflorous), sweet jelly-textured flesh. Slow to bear from seed (7 to 10 yr); grafted 3 to 4 yr.
entries.source: Embrapa Brazil jaboticaba cultivar guide; UF/IFAS jaboticaba guide

windows.notes: Larger fruit than Sabara; thicker skin; sweet rich pulp

entries.notes: Brazilian Sao Paulo selection. Larger fruit than Sabara, thicker skin, rich sweet pulp. Slower to ripen on tree. Hardy briefly to 24F mature.

windows.notes: Pear-shaped jaboticaba; large elongated fruit; very sweet

entries.notes: Brazilian selection. Pear-shaped elongated large fruit, very sweet rich pulp, often considered superior to round types. Slow to bear from seed.

windows.notes: Caribbean Criollo x Forastero hybrid; bulk of fine-flavor cacao; understory

entries.notes: Trinidad hybrid of Criollo and Forastero. Hardier than Criollo, finer flavor than pure Forastero, basis of most fine-flavor cocoa. Needs shade and 80 percent humidity.
entries.source: ICCO cocoa varieties guide; FAO cacao cultivation manual

windows.notes: Amazonian bulk cocoa; 80 percent of world supply; vigorous and disease resistant

entries.notes: Amazonian cacao, dominant world production. Bitter strong chocolate flavor, vigorous, disease resistant. Includes Amelonado and CCN-51 lines. Understory in shade.
entries.source: ICCO cocoa varieties guide; FAO cacao cultivation manual

windows.notes: Original Mesoamerican fine cacao; lowest yield; finest flavor; disease prone

entries.notes: Original Mesoamerican cacao, less than 5 percent of world supply. Finest aromatic flavor, low bitterness, low yield, very susceptible to disease. Highest premium grade.
entries.source: ICCO cocoa varieties guide; FAO cacao cultivation manual

windows.notes: Sweet dark red selection; reduced resin off-flavor; hedge or specimen

entries.notes: Improved Surinam cherry. Dark red almost black sweet fruit, lower resin off-flavor than seedlings, ribbed pumpkin-shaped fruit, twice-yearly crop in Florida. Hardy briefly to 26F.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension Surinam cherry guide

windows.notes: Red and yellow strains exist; hardier than tropical guava; container friendly

entries.notes: Brazilian Cattley guava, distinct species from tropical guava. Small red or yellow fruit, strawberry-pineapple flavor, compact shrub, hardy briefly to 22F mature. Container favorite.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension Cattley guava guide

windows.notes: UC late-season seedless mandarin; large pebbly fruit; harvest Feb to Apr

entries.notes: UC Riverside 1999 release, irradiated from Wilking. Larger than Gold Nugget, pebbly rind, seedless, sweet rich flavor, late-season. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Mandarin x orange natural hybrid; spicy rich flavor; harvest Jan to Mar

entries.notes: Florida heirloom natural hybrid 1916. Deep orange rind, spicy aromatic rich flesh, many seeds, easy peel like mandarin. Less cold-hardy than mandarins.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension citrus cultivar guide

windows.notes: Spanish leading clementine; seedless when isolated; harvest Nov to Jan

entries.notes: Spanish 1953 bud sport of Fina clementine. Most-grown clementine in Spain. Larger fruit than Algerian, seedless when isolated, easy peel, sweet. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Late-season juice orange; holds on tree summer; harvest Mar to Oct

entries.notes: Spanish-Portuguese heirloom introduced California 1870s. Premier juice orange, holds on tree without losing quality, regreens in summer heat. Self-fruitful.

windows.notes: Original navel orange; California heirloom; harvest Dec to Apr

entries.notes: Brazilian Bahia bud sport, propagated 1873 in Washington DC and Riverside CA. Seedless, deep orange, classic dessert orange, basis of California navel industry. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UC Riverside Citrus Variety Collection descriptor

windows.notes: Standard supermarket green lime; seedless triploid; nearly thornless

entries.notes: Persian or Tahiti lime, the dominant commercial lime in temperate markets. Seedless triploid, larger than Mexican lime, hardier briefly to 28F. Self-fruitful.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension lime cultivar guide

windows.notes: Aromatic double-lobed leaves are the primary harvest; bumpy fruit zest used too

entries.notes: Southeast Asian species. Hourglass-shaped double leaves used in Thai and Indonesian cuisine, bumpy fruit rind zested for flavor, juice rarely used. Compact shrub.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension lime cultivar guide

windows.notes: Tropical yellow passionfruit; less cold-hardy than purple; needs cross-pollination

entries.notes: Tropical yellow passionfruit, more vigorous than purple, larger more tart fruit, used for juice processing. Needs cross-pollination by carpenter bees or hand. Frost tender below 32F.

windows.notes: South American hardier than tropical guava; plant 2 for cross-pollination; harvest Oct to Dec

entries.notes: Mammoth feijoa selection. Large fragrant green fruit, pineapple-mint flavor, mostly self-incompatible plant 2 cultivars. Hardy to 15F mature. Edible flowers also.
entries.source: UC ANR feijoa cultivar guide; Lousiana SU pineapple guava guide

windows.notes: Self-fertile feijoa selection; reliable solo planting; California heirloom

entries.notes: California heirloom self-fertile feijoa. Reliable as solo planting unlike most cultivars, medium pear-shaped fruit, sweet pineapple-mint aromatic flesh. Hardy to 15F.

windows.notes: California self-fertile feijoa; large light green fruit; smooth flesh

entries.notes: California self-fertile feijoa. Large fruit, smooth seedless texture, mild sweet, good pollinizer for other feijoas. Hardy to 15F mature.

windows.notes: Florida dwarf condo mango; bears in containers; harvest Jun to Jul

entries.notes: Florida selection. Naturally dwarf 6 to 12 ft, ideal containers, coconut-flavored sweet fiberless flesh, monoembryonic. One of the best condo mangoes.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mango cultivar guide

windows.notes: Chinese giant lychee; large fruit and large seed; flavor variable

entries.notes: Chinese cultivar (Da Zao). Largest lychee fruit at 1.5 to 2 oz, dark red leathery skin, sweet but often large seed. Needs winter chill to flower.
entries.source: U Hawaii CTAHR lychee cultivar guide

windows.notes: Caribbean selection; reduced fiber; large fruit; needs hand pollination

entries.notes: Caribbean soursop selection. Reduced fiber, large heart-shaped spiny green fruit, white aromatic creamy-tart pulp. Hand pollinate for yield. Frost kills below 30F.

windows.notes: Thai precocious sugar apple; large round fruit; sweet custard pulp

entries.notes: Thai improved sugar apple. Large round fruit with bumpy segments, sweet custard-textured white pulp, bears at 2 to 3 yr. Hardy briefly to 28F mature.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension sugar apple cultivar guide

windows.notes: Cuban-Florida selection; salmon-red flesh; sweet pumpkin-vanilla flavor

entries.notes: Cuban-Florida mamey selection. Salmon-red dense flesh, sweet pumpkin-almond-vanilla flavor, very productive. Frost-sensitive below 32F. Bears 4 to 6 yr from grafted plant.
entries.source: UF/IFAS Cooperative Extension mamey sapote guide

windows.notes: Thai pink-tinged sweet cultivar; crisp aril; mid-season

entries.notes: Thai selection. Pink-tinged skin, sweet crisp aril, small seed. Productive in tropics. Some chill helps reliable flowering. Frost-sensitive.

windows.notes: Plant dormant canes early spring

entries.notes: Summer-bearing red, hardy heirloom from 1914. Self-fertile. Reliable in cold climates. Floricane-fruiting, prune two-year canes after harvest.
entries.source: University of Minnesota Extension; Fedco Seeds catalog descriptor

entries.notes: Summer-bearing red, very cold hardy Manitoba selection. Self-fertile. Suckers freely. Good for jam and freezing.
Summer-bearing red, hardy Boyne-type. Self-fertile, firm berries good for fresh market. Mildew resistant.
Summer-bearing red, tolerates heavy soils others struggle in. Self-fertile, mid-season harvest.
Summer-bearing red, large firm berries, root rot tolerant. Excellent for wet Pacific Northwest soils.
Summer-bearing red, long picking season, large glossy berries. Premier fresh-market cultivar. Less hardy than Boyne types.
entries.source: Oregon State University Extension; British Columbia Berry Trials

entries.notes: Summer-bearing red, dark berries, classic Pacific Northwest processing variety. Productive, vigorous canes.
Summer-bearing red, leading processing variety in Washington. Bright red, firm berries, excellent freezer quality.
Summer-bearing purple, spineless Scottish bred. Sweet, novelty color, good for u-pick. Vigorous.
entries.source: James Hutton Institute; Fedco Seeds catalog descriptor

entries.notes: Summer-bearing red, late season, very large firm berries. Spineless. Good shelf life.
Summer-bearing red, mid-season, spineless. Compact habit, good for tunnel production.
Summer-bearing red, very late season extends harvest into August. Large bright berries, excellent flavor.
Summer-bearing red, New Zealand bred. Large firm berries, good disease resistance.
entries.source: Plant and Food Research New Zealand

entries.notes: Primocane fall-bearing red, early ripening even in short seasons. Mow to ground each spring for simpler management.
entries.source: Polish Institute of Pomology; Fedco Seeds catalog descriptor

entries.notes: Primocane fall-bearing red, large firm berries, heavy yields. Mow primocanes after fall harvest for next-year crop.
Primocane fall-bearing red, early everbearer, large dark berries. Self-supporting canes need minimal trellis.
Primocane fall-bearing red, larger and firmer than Autumn Bliss. Strong fall flavor.
Primocane fall-bearing red, Swiss bred, very large berries, root rot tolerant. Needs trellis support.
Primocane fall-bearing red, very early ripening, deep red sweet berries. USDA release.
Primocane fall-bearing red, spineless canes, large firm fruit. Excellent for u-pick.
Primocane fall-bearing red, spineless, slightly later than Joan J. Productive everbearer.
Semi-erect thornless floricane. Large sweet berries late summer. Cold-hardy among thornless types, productive, self-fertile.
entries.source: USDA ARS; Ohio State University Extension

entries.notes: Erect thornless floricane, University of Arkansas release. Self-supporting canes, sweet firm berries.
Erect thornless floricane, earliest ripening Arkansas variety. Small seeds, glossy berries.
Erect thornless floricane, largest fruit of Arkansas thornless line. Mid to late season.
Erect thorny floricane, vigorous, productive. University of Arkansas release.
Erect thorny floricane, early season Arkansas release. Small seeds, excellent flavor.
Erect thorny floricane, very large berries up to 3 inches long. Long harvest window.
Erect thornless floricane, disease resistant including rosette. Firm berries, good shipping quality.
Semi-erect thornless floricane, earliest of Arkansas thornless, very large fruit.
Erect thornless floricane, sweetest of Arkansas line. Mid-season, firm fruit.
Primocane-fruiting thornless. Bears on first-year canes for fall crop. Large berries, prune to favor primocane fruiting.
Primocane-fruiting thorny, commercial shipping quality, firm berries. Fall crop on first-year canes.
Primocane-fruiting thornless with shipping quality. Tip prune for branching and yield.
Trailing thornless, extremely heavy yielder, long harvest. Needs strong trellis. Better adapted to warmer zones.
Trailing thorny floricane, classic Oregon berry, intense flavor. Train canes on two-wire trellis.
Trailing hybrid (blackberry x raspberry x loganberry), reddish-purple, soft melting flesh. Trellis required.
Trailing red-purple hybrid (blackberry x raspberry). Tart flavor, excellent for cooking and wine.
Trailing Scottish hybrid, large dark red berries, aromatic flavor. Vigorous, needs trellis.
Trailing California berry, large glossy black fruit. Mild winter zones only, classic for pies on the central coast.
Trailing thornless from Oregon breeding program. Large glossy black firm berries, productive.
Trailing thorny, very early ripening Oregon variety. Large sweet glossy berries.
Trailing thornless, very large Marion-flavored berries. Productive, machine-harvestable.
Trailing thornless early-season, complementary to Columbia Star. Large firm berries.
Trailing thornless with Pacific trailing blackberry parentage. Intense wild-blackberry flavor.
Northern highbush, very early ripening. Plant with mid and late varieties for extended harvest. Cross-pollinate for best yields.
Northern highbush, very large early berries with excellent flavor. Sensitive to soil pH, needs acidic soil.
entries.source: USDA ARS; Michigan State University Extension

entries.notes: Northern highbush mid-season, very large light blue berries. Concentrated ripening good for u-pick.
Northern highbush, very early, compact bush. Hardy and reliable for short seasons.
Northern highbush mid-season, large flavorful berries. Heavy producer, withstands heat well for a northern type.
entries.source: USDA ARS; Michigan State University Extension

entries.notes: Northern highbush late mid-season, very large light blue berries, mild flavor. Open bush easy to pick.
Northern highbush late season, large tart berries until fully ripe. Excellent flavor when sweet.
Northern highbush late season, very large flavorful berries. Tart-sweet, good for processing.
Northern highbush, largest blueberry on the market, dime-sized fruit. Long six-week harvest window.
entries.source: USDA ARS; New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station

entries.notes: Wild-selected northern highbush, small intensely-flavored berries with highest antioxidant levels.
Northern highbush, latest ripening commercial variety extends season. Large firm berries.
entries.source: USDA ARS; Michigan State University Extension

entries.notes: Northern highbush late season, machine-harvestable, sweet aromatic flavor.
Northern highbush mid-season, firm light-blue berries with excellent shelf life. Commercial favorite.
Half-southern-highbush hybrid, partly evergreen, wider zone adaptability. Sweet flavorful berries.
entries.source: USDA ARS; North Carolina State University

entries.notes: Southern highbush, low chill 400 hours, excellent flavor. Plant with another southern type for cross pollination.
Southern highbush, low chill 200 hours, vigorous. Best for warm winter regions, Florida selection.
Southern highbush, 400 chill hours, large firm berries. Florida release for early commercial harvest.
Southern highbush, 250 chill hours, evergreen in mild winters. Heavy yields, large mild berries.
Southern highbush, 200 chill hours, very early. Tart-sweet flavor, commercial Florida variety.
Southern highbush, 200 chill hours, earliest ripening for warm winters. Florida release.
Southern highbush, 400 chill hours, Georgia release. Firm berries, excellent flavor.
Rabbiteye, early ripening, concentrated harvest. Plant with another rabbiteye for cross pollination.
Rabbiteye, early to mid-season, large light blue berries. Reliable Southern variety.
Rabbiteye, mid to late season, large light blue waxy berries. Crack resistant, vigorous.
Rabbiteye, early to mid-season, vigorous upright bush. Drought tolerant once established.
Rabbiteye, very late season, extends harvest into August. Large flavorful berries.
Half-high northern highbush x lowbush hybrid. Very cold hardy to -35F, spreading habit.
Half-high dwarf, 18 inches tall, excellent for containers and cold climates. Very hardy.
Half-high, 3 feet tall, hardy with large dark berries. Heavy yields in short seasons.
Half-high, 2 feet tall, hardy Minnesota selection. Sweet sky-blue berries.
Half-high early-season, excellent flavor. Minnesota release, hardy to zone 3.
Half-high, 4 feet tall, hardy. Sky-blue berries with excellent flavor. Pollinizer for Polaris.
Half-high early season, hardy. Plant with Polaris for cross pollination, sweet light-blue berries.
Nearly thornless red-pink dessert variety. Mildew resistant, self-fertile, good for fresh eating.
entries.source: Cornell Cooperative Extension; Fedco Seeds catalog descriptor

entries.notes: Few-thorned dusty pink berries, mildew resistant. University of Minnesota release, hardy.
Dark purple-red berries with rich flavor like wild blueberry. Productive, self-fertile.
Thornless red dessert berry, large and sweet. Mildew resistant, easy to pick.
entries.source: European fruit trial; Raintree Nursery catalog descriptor

entries.notes: Mildew-immune red gooseberry, excellent for organic culture. Mid-season ripening.
Wild prairie selection, extremely cold hardy. Large pink-red sweet berries.
Large yellow-green dessert gooseberry, mildew resistant. Sweet when fully ripe.
Early-ripening red currant, long strigs, productive. Dutch heirloom, vigorous upright bush.
Late-ripening red currant, very long strigs, easy to pick. Most productive red currant available.
entries.source: Dutch fruit trial; Raintree Nursery catalog descriptor

entries.notes: Old French variety, very large bright red berries. Productive, self-fertile.
Mild-flavored sweet red currant. Excellent for fresh eating, less tart than typical varieties.
Very productive white currant, sweet mild flavor. Czech selection, excellent for fresh eating.
French heirloom white currant, pale yellow translucent berries. Sweet and aromatic.
Scottish bred mid-season black currant. Large berries, high vitamin C. Mildew resistant.
Compact early-season black currant, very large berries. Good for small gardens.
Big bud mite resistant, productive Scottish variety. Sweet rich flavor, late mid-season.
White pine blister rust immune black currant. Legal to plant in restricted US states. Vigorous.
White pine blister rust immune, productive. Companion to Consort for cross pollination.
English heirloom black currant from 1913. Sweet rich flavor, good for jam and cassis.
Rare French pink currant, translucent salmon berries, sweet flavor between red and white.
Productive American elderberry, large clusters. Plant near Adams II or another variety for best pollination.
Companion pollinator to Adams I, vigorous and productive. Excellent for syrup and wine.
Early ripening, vigorous, large clusters. Excellent pollinator for other American elderberries.
Late ripening Oklahoma selection, very large clusters. Productive for syrup production.
Compact Missouri selection, only 6 feet tall, suited to small spaces. Productive midsize clusters.
Ornamental purple lacy-leaved European elder, pink flowers, edible if cooked. Cross with another European elder for fruit.
entries.source: Missouri Botanical Garden; Proven Winners descriptor

entries.notes: Dark-leaved ornamental European elder, lemon-scented pink flowers. Edible fruit when fully ripe and cooked.
Dutch selection, heavy yielder of tart red berries. Evergreen groundcover, needs acidic soil pH 4-5.
Dutch lingonberry with large dark red berries. Two crops per year possible in cool summers.
Swedish lingonberry, vigorous, large berries with classic tart flavor. Good for cooking.
German selection, vigorous spreader, fall harvest. Excellent for preserves.
entries.source: European fruit trial; Raintree Nursery catalog descriptor

entries.notes: University of Saskatchewan release, large sweet-tart berries. Needs cross-pollinator like Tundra or Borealis.
Tall vigorous pollinator variety. Universal pollen donor for haskap, large berries.
Pollinator variety for Aurora, Tundra, Borealis. Large firm berries, productive.
Dwarf 2-3 foot variety, ideal for containers. Sweet berries, needs Berry Blue or Blue Belle pollinator.
Late season haskap, very large berries. Plant with Boreal Beast for pollination.
Late season pollinator for Boreal Beauty and Boreal Blizzard. Heavy yields of firm sweet berries.
Largest honeyberry variety, blueberry-sized fruit. Late blooming reduces frost risk. Needs Boreal Beast.
Self-fertile sweet-flavored goji. Productive, drought tolerant once established. Train to trellis.
entries.source: Proven Winners descriptor; Cornell Cooperative Extension

entries.notes: Large-fruited goji selection, self-fertile. Best harvested by shaking onto sheet, sweet when fully red.
Improved Chinese goji selection, large sweet berries. Productive, self-fertile, tolerates heat.
Polish commercial selection, very productive. High antioxidant black chokeberries, self-fertile.
USDA NRCS conservation release, vigorous and hardy. Wildlife and erosion control plus fruit.
Russian female cultivar, large orange berries high in vitamin C. Needs male pollinator like Pollmix.
German female cultivar, easier to harvest with loose berries. Needs male pollinator within 50 feet.
Polish male pollinator cultivar, abundant pollen production. Plant one male per 6-8 females.
German female sea buckthorn, vigorous with large orange-red berries. Late maturing, high oil content.
German female cultivar, ornamental and productive. Bright orange berries persist into winter.
Industry standard hybrid cranberry, productive, deep red berries. Requires constantly moist acidic peat soil.
Late-season hybrid, large deep red berries. Productive USDA release, good for home bog plantings.
Classic Massachusetts heirloom from 1843, late season. Small berries store well, holds color through winter.
Massachusetts heirloom, very early ripening, dark almost-black berries. Sweet flavor for fresh use.
Rutgers release, high yields, vibrant deep red color. Suitable for commercial bog production.
University of Wisconsin release, very high anthocyanin, deep red color. Early ripening.
Rutgers release, very high yields, large dark red berries. Excellent commercial variety.
California commercial standard, late leafing reduces frost damage. Cross-pollinate with Franquette for best yields.
Top California commercial walnut, lateral-bearing for high yields. Bears in 4-5 years, large light-colored kernels.
French heirloom, very late leafing avoids spring frost. Excellent flavor, classic Oregon variety.
Lateral-bearing California variety, precocious yields. Large nuts with light kernels, commercial favorite.
Cold hardy Eastern European strain, hardy to -30F. Self-fertile but produces better with another seedling nearby.

Roots harvested year 1 or 2. Blood-moving herb in TCM, directs herbs downward. Treat as annual north of zone 7.
Sichuan species; roots are stronger blood movers than Achyranthes. Used in TCM for back and joint pain. Rich loam, partial shade.
Epiphytic orchid; stems harvested year 2+. Yin tonic in TCM for stomach and lung. Mount on bark or grow in coarse orchid mix.
Whole plant used cautiously in TCM as warming wind-dispelling herb. Contains aristolochic acid; cultivate only with informed guidance.
White-flowered medicinal selection for tea. Cools liver and eyes in TCM. Harvest flowers fully open in fall and dry quickly out of light.
Tree; bark harvested from trunks 15+ years old. Qi-moving and calming in TCM. Slow grower; deep moist soil, light shade when young.
Aerial parts harvested mid summer. Heat-clearing antimicrobial in TCM; pungent fish-mint flavor. Aggressive runner; contain in pots or moist bed.
Chinese mugwort used for moxibustion. Aerial parts harvested just before flowering. Spreads vigorously by rhizome; contain in bed.
Purple-leaf medicinal form; leaves and seeds release exterior and move qi in TCM. Self-seeds; distinct from culinary green shiso.
High alpine plant; rhizomes harvested year 3+. Wind-cold dispelling in TCM. Needs cool summers and cold winters; struggles below 4000 ft.
Tubers used only after extensive processing in TCM; raw tubers are toxic. Phlegm transforming. Shade-loving; spreads by bulbils.
Roots harvested year 2 or 3. Shen-calming and lung-opening in TCM. Dry slopes in nature; sandy well-drained soil, full sun.
Nan wu wei zi; redder fruit, milder than S. chinensis. Climbing vine; trellis needed. Lung and kidney tonic in TCM.
Asiatic dogwood; fruit harvested late fall after first frost. Kidney yin tonic in TCM. Small tree; produces fruit after 5 to 7 years.
Fruit harvested fall, sliced and dried. Digestive aid in TCM for fatty meat stagnation. Tree fruits at 5+ years; cold hardy.
Red dates dried for TCM use as harmonizing spleen tonic. Distinct medicinal selections from culinary types; pick fully ripe and sun-dry.
Fruit harvested fall, used to release exterior wind-heat for headache in TCM. Shrubby; full sun, drought tolerant once established.
Vining perennial; fruit, seed, peel, and root all used distinctly in TCM. Trellis required; full sun. Roots harvested year 2 or 3.
Seeds harvested fall, roasted for tea. Liver-clearing and bowel-moving in TCM. Self-sows; can become weedy in warm zones.
Parasitic vine; seeds harvested fall. Kidney yang tonic in TCM. Requires a host plant (often soybean) to mature; quarantine cultivation.
Flower buds harvested just before opening for TCM use as heat-clearing antimicrobial. Vigorous vine; trellis required. Distinct medicinal harvest from ornamental.
Fruit capsules harvested fall, dried for TCM use as heat-clearing antimicrobial. Distinct from F. suspensa lian qiao ornamental harvest pattern.
Aerial parts harvested just before flowering. Wind-heat releasing in TCM. Aggressive spreader; contain in bottomless pot or buried barrier.
Roots harvested year 2 or 3. Wind-dispelling herb in TCM; eases joint pain. Cold-tolerant; sandy soil, full sun, low water.
Tuberous root segments harvested year 2 or 3. Yin tonic for lung and stomach in TCM. Evergreen groundcover; partial shade preferred.
Rhizomes harvested fall year 3+. Gentle yin tonic in TCM and Western herbalism. Shade-loving; humus-rich soil.
Roots harvested year 2 or 3. Lung-opening expectorant in TCM. Self-seeds in disturbed ground; full sun to part shade.
Northern bupleurum; roots stronger than B. scorzonerifolium. Liver-soothing in TCM. Sun, sandy loam, drought tolerant.
Same plant as sheng di huang; the prepared (nine-times steamed) form is the major blood tonic in TCM. Grow for processing into shu di huang.
Slow woodland perennial; rhizomes harvested year 5+. Powerful bitter heat-clearing herb in TCM, parallels goldenseal. Deep shade, moist humus.
Cold-hardy huang jing alternative. Sweet rhizome, qi and yin tonic in TCM, traditionally cooked into porridge. Spreads slowly.
Glossy privet fruit harvested fall. Liver and kidney yin tonic in TCM. Small evergreen tree; tolerates urban pollution.
Bark harvested from 10+ year trees. Yang tonic for liver and kidney in TCM. Hardy tree containing rubber latex in bark; full sun.
Black ripe fruit harvested early summer as TCM blood tonic. Distinct from culinary mulberry use. Bark (sang bai pi) and leaves also medicinal.
Peeled boiled root of white-flowered selections used in TCM as bai shao for blood nourishment. Harvest roots fall year 3 or 4.
Unpeeled raw roots from red-flowered wild-type peonies used in TCM as chi shao for blood movement. Distinct preparation from bai shao.
Root bark harvested year 4+. Heat-clearing blood-cooling herb in TCM. Woody shrub peony; deep loose soil with good drainage.
Aerial parts harvested when plant blooms. Yang tonic in TCM. Shade-loving evergreen groundcover; rich moist soil.
Long air-potato yam; tubers harvested fall. Spleen and lung qi tonic in TCM. Vigorous vine; trellis required. Invasive in southeast US.
Aquatic; rhizomes harvested late fall. Drains damp in TCM. Plant in shallow water or saturated soil at pond margin.

Flowers harvested year 2+. Cooling herb in Siddha and Ayurveda; tea for diabetes support. Shrub to 6 ft; drought tolerant established.
